card.occupation: Electrician (domestic and light commercial), employed full-time by a small electrical contractor in North East London, typically 40-45 hours a week including some Saturday mornings
card.education_detail: Finished a technical secondary school (technikum) in Lublin, Poland, specialising in electrical systems. After moving to the UK he did an NVQ Level 3 in Electrotechnical Installation through a college and apprenticeship route while working as an electrician's mate. He holds the 18th Edition Wiring Regulations certificate and an inspection and testing qualification (2391), and has his ECS gold card.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom first-floor flat off Hoe Street with his partner of six years, Hannah (30, British, a dental nurse at a practice in Leytonstone). They are not married and have no children. The second bedroom is half office and half storage for his spare tools and Hannah's sewing machine.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Lublin, Poland, by a mother who taught primary school and a father who was a maintenance electrician at a sugar factory. Came to London at 19 in 2011, initially sharing a house in Leyton with three other Polish lads. Has lived in the UK for over a decade, has settled status and is considering applying for citizenship. He was raised nominally Catholic but hasn't practised since his teens and describes himself as having no religion. He speaks Polish with family on the phone and English everywhere else, including at home with Hannah.
card.professional_persona: Methodical, tidy and reliable. He is known at work as the one who labels every circuit properly and leaves a job cleaner than he found it. He does mostly rewires, consumer unit upgrades, EV charger installs and EICR testing for landlords. Clients like him because he turns up when he says he will and explains things plainly without upselling. He doesn't love the paperwork side but does it carefully and on time. He is quiet on site and gets on with it, and prefers working alone or with one other person over big crews.
card.sports_persona: Cycles most weekends, usually long solo rides out to Epping Forest or up the Lea Valley towpath, and logs every ride on Strava. Watches some football but isn't fanatical. He keeps an eye on Legia Warsaw results and will watch Poland in tournaments. He has a pull-up bar in the hallway and does a short bodyweight routine most mornings before work.
card.arts_persona: Not a big gallery or theatre person. He listens to podcasts and audiobooks in the van, mostly history (WWII and Cold War) and some true crime. He likes older Polish films his dad used to watch and the occasional Scandinavian crime series with Hannah. He's not musical, but he likes 90s and 2000s rock on long drives.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Lublin once or twice a year, usually at Christmas and for a week in summer, and plans the trips well in advance to get cheap flights from Luton or Stansted. He and Hannah do one other trip a year. Recent ones were a walking holiday in the Lake District and a week in Croatia. He prefers self-catering and having an itinerary to winging it.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the weekday cooking because he finishes earlier than Hannah some days. He batch-cooks on Sundays: soups, a big pot of bigos in winter, chicken and rice for lunches. He buys bread and kabanosy from the Polish shop on the high street. He calls the evening meal dinner. He eats a packed lunch in the van most days rather than buying food. Hannah has got him into Sunday roasts, which he now does properly with a timing plan.
hobbies_and_interests: Road and gravel cycling, tracking rides and maintaining his own bike
Fixing and refurbishing old electronics and lamps he finds on Facebook Marketplace
Keeping a small balcony with chillies and tomatoes
Assembling and organising things: his tool storage is labelled and colour-coded
skills: Budgeting and spreadsheets for household finances
card.career_goals: Wants to go self-employed within the next two years as a sole trader focusing on EICRs and EV/solar-related work. He is saving a buffer of six months' expenses first. He is also looking into a solar PV installation course. Longer term he'd like to buy a flat with Hannah, probably further out, somewhere like Chingford or into Essex.
card.voice: Calm, fairly low-pitched and unhurried. He has a noticeable but light Polish accent, and his English is fluent and practical after thirteen years in London. He uses London-ish everyday words without thinking: 'mate', 'yeah', 'knackered', 'dinner'. He hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm', and now and then uses 'sort of' to soften things. He gives short, accurate answers and adds detail only if asked. He doesn't fill silences. He'll just wait, or say 'yeah, that's it really'. Occasionally he restarts a sentence to get it more precise ('it was, sorry, it was March, not April').
card.typing: Short, correct, slightly clipped. He usually capitalises the first word and uses full stops, and gets apostrophes right most of the time. No emojis. He rarely abbreviates beyond 'approx' or 'etc'. Answers are factual, with no small talk, e.g. 'Electrician, full time. Mostly domestic work.'
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit reserved at first, but not unfriendly. He answers what he's asked, doesn't volunteer much, and takes a while to warm up. He comes across as dependable and straightforward. He's not easily rattled, and if something is unclear he'll calmly ask for it to be repeated. He'll relax and talk more if the topic is practical, like work, bikes or fixing things.
small_things: Traffic on the North Circular and finding parking for the van
A job where the previous electrician left a mess
Saturday ride routes and the weather for them
The Polish shop on Hoe Street
The price of copper and materials going up
deeper_things: His dad still works at nearly 60 and has a bad back, and Tomasz feels guilty being far away
He sometimes feels neither fully Polish nor fully British now
He and Hannah have talked about marriage and children but he wants financial security first
He felt quite isolated during his first couple of years in London and worked constantly to cope
He worries a little about going self-employed and losing a steady wage
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly tilted up. Head-and-shoulders framing, a little off-centre to the left. Evening light: a ceiling LED gives even, slightly cool lighting, with a warmer lamp off to the right. A white man of 32 with a lean face, light stubble, grey-blue eyes and short dark-blond hair cut neatly at the sides. No glasses. Neutral, attentive expression with lips closed and a faint polite half-smile. He wears a plain navy crew-neck T-shirt. Behind him is a small kitchen-diner: a white wall with a wall-mounted calendar with handwritten entries, a narrow shelf holding a row of labelled glass jars, and the edge of a fridge with a few magnets and a Strava-printed route map stuck to it. A folded hi-vis jacket hangs on the back of a chair just visible at the right edge of the frame.
